speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the exact location of your pain and whether it has moved to your right lower quadrant? Also, have you experienced any fever, nausea, or changes in your bowel movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mesenteric Ischemia

Given your recent myocardial infarction and the classic presentation of umbilical pain out of proportion to physical exam findings with bloody stools, this is highly suspicious for acute mesenteric ischemia. We need to confirm this immediately; REQUEST TEST: Lactate_level and REQUEST TEST: CT_Angiography_Abdomen_Pelvis.
